name: [WEEKLY] Web-Facing Service Process Writes to RCE/Persistence Paths (Path-Traversal File-Write)
description: Detects a public-facing server process (Python web/AI app, Java/Tomcat, Node, nginx/httpd, php-fpm) creating or modifying a file OUTSIDE its expected working directory and INSIDE an RCE- or persistence-enabling location — cron drop-ins, ~/.ssh/authorized_keys, shell rc files, Python site-/dist-packages, or a web-root script (.jsp/.php/.aspx). This fortnight a cluster of arbitrary-file-write / path-traversal flaws in AI and comms tooling drove it: Crawl4AI's /screenshot,/pdf output_path traversal and crawler-download traversal (GHSA-365w-hqf6-vxfg, GHSA-2jq4-q6vv-4cp3), Langflow's unauthenticated upload and BaseFileComponent file primitives (CVE-2026-55450, CVE-2026-55447), PraisonAI's unvalidated multiedit tool (GHSA-29w3-p9w9-wc47), gemini-mcp-tool @file/cmd injection (CVE-2026-0755), and the actively-exploited Cisco Unified CM file-write-to-root chain (CVE-2026-20230) that drops a JSP webshell. It spans the exploit→install/persistence kill-chain stages: the public app is abused for write primitive, then the bytes land where they grant code execution or footholds. It FIRES when a long-lived service identity writes to these high-value paths; it does NOT fire on package managers (apt/pip/dpkg), legitimate deploy/CI agents, or interactive admin shells, which are filtered out. Reference IOCs (`<c2_domain_list>`, `<sha256_list>`) are substitution slots only — the detection keys on the write-target + writing-process behaviour, not on rotating hashes.
query: Image:(*created* OR *modified* OR *\/etc\/crontab* OR *authorized_keys* OR *crontab* OR *python* OR *python3* OR *java* OR *node* OR *httpd* OR *nginx* OR *tomcat* OR *uwsgi* OR *gunicorn* OR *php\-fpm*)
